WM.thesis_one_line: America's largest waste hauler and landfill owner, compounding price ahead of cost, but priced richly while it digests a large medical-waste acquisition.
kill_criteria: Core price minus WM's own cash-cost inflation turns negative for two consecutive quarters (the sector's central 'is the moat still working' test; not yet observed - Q2'26 core price +5.7% still comfortably ahead of cost).
Sector-adjusted net debt/EBITDA (reported net debt + landfill/remediation liabilities, divided by adjusted EBITDA) exceeds 3.5x for two consecutive quarters (currently ~3.2x).
FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance (currently $8.15-8.25bn) is cut in dollar terms (not just margin-adjusted) at the Q3'26 (Oct 27, 2026) or later release.
A material adverse development in the Stericycle DOJ deferred-prosecution matter (beyond the already-disclosed penalty) or a new SEC/DOJ inquiry tied to Healthcare Solutions.
Collection & Disposal volume decline exceeds 2% for two consecutive quarters excluding the disclosed wildfire-comparison effect (i.e., volume loss broadens beyond the flagged residential shedding).
key_adverse_facts: Stericycle (wholly owned since Nov 2024) entered a one-year DOJ deferred prosecution agreement in May 2026 over pre-acquisition (2015-2020) conduct at its now-divested controlled-substances business; paid penalty/settlement amounts and remains under ongoing compliance/reporting obligations.

GAAP-to-adjusted operating income gap widened sharply in Q3'25 ($989m GAAP vs $1,241m adjusted, a 25% adjustment) and stayed elevated through Q1-Q2'26, driven by Stericycle integration/restructuring costs.
Q2'26 release cut FY2026 revenue guidance ~0.6% (to $26,275-26,475m from $26,425-26,625m) on lower volume expectations, one quarter after reaffirming the original range.
Collection & Disposal volume declined 1.8% YoY in Q2'26 (partly wildfire-comparison, but also intentional shedding of low-margin residential business).
data_conflicts: d4 quant snapshot shows WM beta = 0.203 (vol_1y 0.203), which looks unusually low for an issuer carrying $23.4bn of total debt; not independently verified against a primary source since beta is a vendor-computed statistic, not an SEC-disclosed figure. Flagged as a possible data-quality issue affecting the b1 composite score's apparent 'quality' read.
WM.confidence_in_thesis: medium - the route-density/landfill-permit moat and RNG/Stericycle growth legs are real and durable, but the premium multiple (12.9x EV/EBITDA, 21.9x P/FCF) and unresolved integration-cost trajectory limit conviction to half-size.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for WM in outputs/v1_valuation_table.csv or v1_valuation.json, so v1_verdict is null and no reconciliation against V1 is possible. My own reverse DCF (WACC 7.0%, terminal growth 3.0%, base FCF = FY2026-guided midpoint $3.8bn) implies ~4.0%/year FCF growth for 10 years, which sits below my own evidence-based base case of ~6-7%/year (mid-single-digit core price plus RNG/Stericycle synergy ramp plus buybacks) - i.e. implied_vs_base = below, satisfying the INCLUDE-SMALL threshold, though the multiple itself (12.9x EV/EBITDA) is not cheap in absolute terms.

WM.scenario_basis: TTM adjusted diluted EPS $7.74 (sum of last 4 quarters: 1.98+1.93+1.81+2.02); current P/E ~26.7x; bear 2%/yr EPS growth + 19x exit P/E, base 7%/yr + 24x exit P/E, bull 11%/yr + 27x exit P/E; plus WM's current 1.8%/yr dividend yield added each year (not reinvested/compounded), annualised over 3 years.

AMCR.thesis_one_line: Newly merged Amcor-Berry is the world's largest consumer-packaging maker, cheap on paper, but it just missed its own (already-cut) cash-flow guidance.
kill_criteria: Leverage (net debt / [LTM adjusted EBITDA + SBC], company's own metric) exceeds 3.8x at any quarter-end (vs the 3.5-3.6x management is itself targeting for Dec-2026).

Free cash flow for the six-month Transition Period (Jul-Dec 2026) comes in below the low end of whatever range management guides at the next release - a second consecutive FCF miss would be a much stronger signal than the first.
Quarterly dividend is cut or held flat for more than 2 consecutive quarters after being raised in FY2026 (a de facto signal management judges coverage to be tight).
Disclosed cost synergies fall below the 'upper end of expectations' pace management has claimed every quarter to date (i.e., synergy realization guidance itself is cut).
The Brazil tax litigation reasonably-possible-loss estimate (currently $27m above the $14m accrual) is revised materially upward in a future filing.
key_adverse_facts: FY2026 free cash flow was $1,303m, below even the ALREADY-CUT guidance range of $1.5-1.6bn given at Q3 FY26 (May 2026), which itself was cut from the original $1.8-1.9bn guided at Q1/Q2 FY26 - a real, quantified, two-step-down cash-flow miss in the first full post-merger fiscal year.

Leverage (net debt / [LTM adjusted EBITDA + SBC]) is targeted by management itself to stay at 3.5x-3.6x through December 31, 2026 - i.e. no meaningful deleveraging is guided for at least another 12+ months.
FY2026 dividends paid ($1,195m) were barely covered by FY2026 free cash flow ($1,303m) in the same year FCF missed guidance - a real coverage-quality flag.

The b1 model's bullish composite score (0.685, decile 7) is driven almost entirely by earnings-momentum/SUE factors that are a mechanical artefact of merger accounting (comparing a combined entity against a much smaller pre-merger base), not organic acceleration; this signal should fade once FY2026 comparisons fully lap.
data_conflicts: d4 quant snapshot's next_earnings_date for AMCR (2026-11-05, flagged as an estimate) is very likely stale: Amcor has publicly announced a fiscal-year-end change from June 30 to December 31, with a standalone six-month 'Transition Period' (July 1-December 31, 2026) report to follow, not a normal quarterly release around early November 2026.
AMCR.next_earnings_date: not applicable (fiscal-year transition) - next disclosure is a six-month Transition Period report (Jul-Dec 2026), expected in early 2027; see data_conflicts
AMCR.confidence_in_thesis: medium - synergy capture has beaten or matched the upper end of plan every quarter disclosed, but the FCF miss and the leverage plateau through year-end are real, unresolved risks that need at least one more clean quarter (or the Transition Period report) to verify.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for AMCR. My own reverse DCF (WACC 7.8%, terminal growth 2.5%) implies ~5.8%/year FCF growth for 10 years on the unadjusted FY2026 actual FCF base ($1,303m, itself depressed by ~$290m of one-off integration costs), or ~3.1%/year on a normalized FCF base (~$1.6bn, adding back those one-offs). Against a plausible 5-6%/year base case (synergy ramp plus modest volume/price growth), the normalized reading is below base case (implied_vs_base = below); the unadjusted reading would be roughly in line. I use the normalized view as primary per earnings-quality practice (one-off costs should not permanently depress the base), which supports the INCLUDE-SMALL threshold, but flag this as a genuine judgement call and the single biggest swing factor in the valuation read.

AMCR.scenario_basis: FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS $4.02 (post 1-for-5 reverse split); current P/E ~10.6x; bear 0%/yr EPS growth + 8x exit P/E, base 7%/yr + 10.5x exit P/E, bull 13%/yr + 12.5x exit P/E; plus AMCR's current 6.1%/yr dividend yield added each year (not reinvested/compounded), annualised over 3 years.

BALL.thesis_one_line: A pure-play global aluminum-can maker riding the plastic-to-aluminum substitution wave, growing double-digit EPS with a credible guidance track record.
kill_criteria: Global aluminum packaging shipment growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (currently +4.3% in Q2'26 - a clean, quantifiable proxy for the substitution thesis losing steam).
Net debt/comparable EBITDA (company's own next disclosed figure) exceeds 3.5x at any year-end or half-year disclosure (currently ~2.8x at Dec 2025, ~3.2x on my own approximation for June 2026).
FY2026 comparable diluted EPS growth guidance (currently '10-plus percent') is cut below 10% at any quarterly update.
The U.S. CBP aluminum-tariff-classification matter (disclosed Sept 2025, unreserved) results in a quantified assessment exceeding $100 million.
Full-year free cash flow for 2026 comes in below the guided $900 million floor at year-end.
key_adverse_facts: An unresolved, unreserved U.S. Customs and Border Protection challenge (notice received Sept 2025) to the tariff classification of certain aluminum imports; Ball states it 'is unable to develop a reasonable estimate of loss' and has recorded no reserve.

FY2026 guidance ('10-plus percent' comparable EPS growth) is a deliberate deceleration from FY2025's delivered ~14% growth; two quarters of 14-22% YoY growth in H1 2026 have not yet prompted a guidance raise.
FY2025 capital returns to shareholders ($1.54bn) exceeded FY2025 free cash flow ($956m), funded partly by balance-sheet/debt capacity.
data_conflicts: Triage (Q13) cited net debt/EBITDA of 3.4x for Ball; my primary-source figure from the company's own disclosed leverage table (FY2025 year-end, 10-Q Note) is net debt $5,800m / comparable EBITDA $2,044m = ~2.8x - meaningfully lower than triage's 3.4x. Source of the discrepancy not identified (possibly an earlier or differently-scoped data snapshot); flagged for lead reconciliation.
BALL.confidence_in_thesis: high - a clean FY2025 guidance-delivery track record, a structural multi-year volume tailwind visible in every reported geographic segment, and a reverse-DCF that does not require aggressive growth assumptions, tempered only by the unquantified tariff contingency.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 systematic-valuation row exists for BALL. My own reverse DCF (WACC 7.5%, terminal growth 2.5%, base FCF = FY2025 actual $956m) implies ~3.8%/year firm-level FCF growth for 10 years. A reasonable base case (2-4%/year global can-volume growth plus modest margin/mix improvement) is ~4-5%/year, so implied growth sits at or slightly below base case (implied_vs_base = below), satisfying the INCLUDE threshold, though with a thinner margin of safety than WM or AMCR's reverse-DCF reads.

BALL.scenario_basis: TTM comparable diluted EPS $3.90 (sum of last 4 quarters: 1.02+0.91+0.94+1.03); current P/E ~14.6x; bear 3%/yr EPS growth + 13x exit P/E, base 11%/yr + 16x exit P/E, bull 16%/yr + 18x exit P/E; plus BALL's current 1.4%/yr dividend yield added each year (not reinvested/compounded), annualised over 3 years.
